request.spec:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Sign-in by name and loading a sheet by id now work on the one screen at `/`. `bin/e2e` passes: the test signs in as uma and then as vic in a second browser, both on the same sheet, and checks each one's name and sheet id after a reload.

**Server**
- A new `sheet` table (`V1__sheet.sql`) records each sheet id and who first loaded it.
- `POST /api/sheets/{id}/load` returns the sheet, creating it if the id has never been used, so a new sheet starts empty. If two users start the same sheet at the same moment, both get the same sheet.
- The code is in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/sheet/`.

**Front end**
- `core/session.ts` holds the signed-in name and the active sheet. It sends the name with every request in an `X-User` header. If two loads overlap, the most recent one is the one shown.
- `features/home/home.ts` shows a sign-in form until you sign in. After that it shows your name (`current-user`), the sheet-id input and Load button (`sheet-id-input`, `sheet-load`), and the active sheet id (`sheet-current-id`).

**Worth knowing**
- **Sign-in is front-end only.** There is no password, as the request says, and the server never checks the name; it just takes whatever arrives in `X-User`.
- **Sign-in isn't remembered.** Refreshing the browser goes back to the sign-in form.
- **Error messages I added.** An empty name or empty sheet id shows an error element (`signin-error` / `sheet-error`), and so does a failed load. The test doesn't check these.
- **No audit records.** Signing in and loading a sheet don't write to the audit file, because the test doesn't expect any.
